title: Cloud-Native CI/CD Pipelines, Tekton & DORA Engineering
summary: Master cloud-native CI/CD pipelines: declarative Tekton Tasks and Pipelines, workspace volume caching, GitHub Actions workflows, DORA metric instrumentation, and automated container build promotion.
learningObjectives: Construct declarative Kubernetes-native CI pipelines using Tekton Task and Pipeline custom resources.
Configure pipeline workspace caching and parameter bindings to accelerate build and test execution cycles.
Instrument DORA deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change failure rate, and MTTR telemetry.

curriculumModules.title: Tekton Pipeline Architecture: Tasks, Workspaces & PipelineRuns
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Tekton provides Kubernetes-native CI/CD primitives. A Task defines an ordered sequence of container steps executing in a shared Pod. Pipelines compose Tasks via explicit runAfter dependencies, passing parameters and sharing state through Workspaces backed by PersistentVolumeClaims or emptyDir.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Isolate build steps in ephemeral rootless containers, persist intermediate build artifacts in dedicated cache volumes, and enforce pipeline concurrency limits to avoid cluster node starvation.

curriculumModules.title: DORA Metrics & Enterprise Pipeline Governance
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: DORA (DevOps Research and Assessment) benchmarks organizational delivery velocity using four metrics: Deployment Frequency, Lead Time for Changes, Time to Restore Service (MTTR), and Change Failure Rate. Automated pipelines emit deployment telemetry on successful releases.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Tag git releases with semantic versions upon pipeline completion, publish deployment events to Prometheus or Webhooks, and gate promotions through automated staging canary verification.

labs.title: Authoring Declarative Tekton Tasks and Pipelines
labs.scenario: Deploy a cloud-native build pipeline in namespace tekton-pipelines: create a Tekton Task build-image that runs step build-container with image crictl:latest, and create a Tekton Pipeline app-ci-pipeline referencing Task build-image with workspace shared-workspace.
labs.productionContext: Tekton decouples CI workflows from proprietary SaaS runners, running directly on Kubernetes with fine-grained RBAC, native secret management, and elastic pod autoscaling.
objectives: Deploy Tekton Task build-image in namespace tekton-pipelines.
Deploy Tekton Pipeline app-ci-pipeline in namespace tekton-pipelines.
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: tekton.dev/v1
kind: Task
metadata:
  name: build-image
  namespace: tekton-pipelines
spec:
  steps:
    - name: build-container
      image: crictl:latest
      command: ['echo', 'Building container image']
---
apiVersion: tekton.dev/v1
kind: Pipeline
metadata:
  name: app-ci-pipeline
  namespace: tekton-pipelines
spec:
  workspaces:
    - name: shared-workspace
  tasks:
    - name: build-step
      taskRef:
        name: build-image

steps.title: Create namespace tekton-pipelines
steps.instruction: Create the dedicated namespace tekton-pipelines for CI workloads.

steps.title: Apply Tekton Task and Pipeline manifest
steps.instruction: Save the Task and Pipeline specifications to /ci/tekton-pipeline.yaml and apply to the cluster.

validationRules.description: Task build-image exists in namespace tekton-pipelines
validationRules.name: build-image
validationRules.remediation: Deploy Task build-image in namespace tekton-pipelines

validationRules.description: Pipeline app-ci-pipeline exists in namespace tekton-pipelines
validationRules.name: app-ci-pipeline
validationRules.remediation: Deploy Pipeline app-ci-pipeline in namespace tekton-pipelines

solutionCommands:
cat << 'EOF' > /ci/tekton-pipeline.yaml
apiVersion: tekton.dev/v1
kind: Task
metadata:
  name: build-image
  namespace: tekton-pipelines
spec:
  steps:
    - name: build-container
      image: crictl:latest
      command: ['echo', 'Building container image']
---
apiVersion: tekton.dev/v1
kind: Pipeline
metadata:
  name: app-ci-pipeline
  namespace: tekton-pipelines
spec:
  workspaces:
    - name: shared-workspace
  tasks:
    - name: build-step
      taskRef:
        name: build-image
EOF

troubleshootingGuide.problem: Tekton resources not found in tekton-pipelines namespace.
troubleshootingGuide.cause: The manifest omitted metadata.namespace or namespace was not created.
troubleshootingGuide.solution: Create the namespace first and ensure metadata.namespace is tekton-pipelines.

labs.title: Configuring CI Workflow Build Caching & Artifact Upload
labs.scenario: Configure a production GitHub Actions CI pipeline: create directory .github/workflows and author ci-build.yml with jobs.build, steps utilizing actions/cache@v4 for dependency caching, and npm test execution.
labs.productionContext: Build caching in continuous integration pipelines reduces test latency by up to 70%, preventing redundant dependency downloads and accelerating developer feedback loops.
objectives: Create directory .github/workflows in the repository root.
Author .github/workflows/ci-build.yml with actions/cache and npm test steps.
labs.starterManifest:
name: CI Pipeline
on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Cache Node Modules
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.npm
          key: npm-cache-${{ hashFiles('package-lock.json') }}
      - name: Run Unit Tests
        run: npm test

steps.title: Create workflow directory
steps.instruction: Create directory .github/workflows for the CI workflow definition.

steps.title: Author workflow definition
steps.instruction: Write the GitHub Actions workflow to .github/workflows/ci-build.yml with actions/cache and npm test.

solutionCommands:
cat << 'EOF' > .github/workflows/ci-build.yml
name: CI Pipeline
on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Cache Node Modules
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.npm
          key: npm-cache-${{ hashFiles('package-lock.json') }}
      - name: Run Unit Tests
        run: npm test
EOF

troubleshootingGuide.problem: Validation fails on missing cache action or npm test step.
troubleshootingGuide.cause: The file was saved to the wrong directory or omitted required steps.
troubleshootingGuide.solution: Ensure .github/workflows/ci-build.yml exists and contains actions/cache@v4 and npm test.

assessmentQuestions.question: What is the primary architectural difference between a Tekton Task and a Tekton Pipeline?
options: A Task compiles Go code while a Pipeline only packages Docker images.
A Task defines an ordered sequence of container steps executing in a single Pod, whereas a Pipeline orchestrates multiple Tasks as a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) across Pods.
Tasks run exclusively on virtual machines while Pipelines run on Kubernetes.
A Task is deprecated in favor of Kubernetes CronJobs.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: In Tekton, a Task executes sequential steps inside a single Pod sharing an emptyDir workspace. A Pipeline orders multiple Tasks using runAfter and shares data across Tasks using Workspaces.

assessmentQuestions.question: Which DORA metric measures the time elapsed from code commit to successful production deployment?
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Lead Time for Changes tracks the duration required for a committed code change to reach production. High-performing engineering teams achieve a lead time of less than one day.
